item.title: Budget 2027 speech tonight: Finance Minister Caruana to address the nation from 6.30pm
item.description: Finance Minister Clyde Caruana is due to deliver the Budget 2027 address tonight, with the speech set to begin at 6.30pm. Newsbook Malta and RTK103 say they will carry live updates online and on radio throughout the evening.

item.title: Budget 2027: Caruana to present the budget this evening as the superbonus question hangs over the government
item.description: Finance Minister Clyde Caruana is scheduled to deliver the Budget 2027 address at 6.30pm, after presenting the package to President Myriam Spiteri Debono at 5pm and entering Parliament at 5.45pm. The most closely watched measure is Labour's pledged €1,000 yearly superbonus for workers, with Caruana indicating taxpayers may have to wait while government messaging has stayed deliberately coy. He has also said the deficit cannot rise beyond 3% of GDP, even as energy subsidies cost up to €400 million a year, with a further €400 million allocated for next year. Prime Minister Robert Abela has said tax cuts for working parents will double and that pensioners are in line for an extra €10 a week, while Times of Malta, Newsbook Malta, The Malta Independent and Malta Today are all running live coverage of the announcements through the evening.

item.title: Social security benefit spending up 10% in first nine months of 2026
item.description: National data published on Monday show spending on social security benefits between January and September reached €1,329.2 million, 10% more than the €1,208.2 million recorded by the same point in 2025. Non-contributory benefits accounted for €1,042.4 million, a 9.5% rise, while contributory spending grew by €90.8 million. Retirement pensions recorded the largest increase, at €60.3 million, driven by a €73.5 million rise in the two-thirds pension, and the number of two-thirds pensioners reached 65,543, 2,690 more than last year. Child allowance also rose by €10.9 million after the grant was extended to families with children in years 10 and 11.

item.title: Jurors shown video of the route retraced by murder accused Lorin Scicluna
item.description: Jurors in the Lassana Cisse murder trial were on Monday shown footage of a journey carried out by police with the accused, Lorin Scicluna, retracing the route he allegedly took on the night of the killing. The video was recorded on 19 May 2019, two days after his arrest, and was played during the testimony of police superintendent Josric Mifsud, who accompanied him. It showed officers driving with Scicluna from the Attard pastizzeria where he worked, along the Marsa-Ħamrun bypass and through Paola, where he had a garage, and places he indicated he collected a firearm and removed his car's registration plates.

item.title: Murder trial opens with evidence compilation in the case of John Cassar
item.description: Evidence compilation opened on Monday before Magistrate Ingrid Bianco in the case of John Cassar, 47, a resident of Siġġiewi accused of the murder of his mother, Mary Grace Cassar, 72, and the attempted murder of his father, also known as Ġanni, 74. The alleged killing took place on 15 October at a residence in Imqabba. Cassar pleaded not guilty to the charges and was remanded in custody. During the hearing, the prosecution began examining the evidence and witnesses so that the court can determine whether there is sufficient proof to send the accused to trial, and ultimately to the jury.

item.title: Disciplinary proceedings against magistrate Monica Vella have begun
item.description: Judicial authorities have opened disciplinary proceedings against Magistrate Monica Vella over alleged inefficiency in handling cases, including extensive delays and other administrative failings. Vella will be given the opportunity to respond, and if the shortcomings are confirmed she could face measures ranging from suspension to removal from the bench. Court statistics issued in August show she had 1,672 pending criminal cases, second only to Magistrate Yana Micallef Stafrace, with more than 93% of them district-related cases. She was suspended from the bench for a month last year over delays in issuing written sentences, and a constitutional court has separately referred a case she presided over to the standards commissioner for the judiciary.

item.title: Man gets suspended sentence over unauthorised passports and is ordered deported to Lebanon
item.description: Sadek Hamze, 53, admitted in court on Monday to attempting to travel to Germany with unauthorised passports for himself, his wife and their two young children, seeking a better life for his family. He pleaded guilty to all charges and was sentenced to two years in prison, suspended for four years, and fined €450, with the court ordering his deportation to Lebanon. The case surfaced when a boarding agent at the airport noticed the documents did not match the identities of the people presenting them. Magistrate Tanya Sammut expressed concern over whether the family could face conflict in Lebanon, with an interpreter noting the fighting is concentrated in the south of the country, near the Israeli border.

item.title: Momentum says request for information on Gozo valley works was refused
item.description: Momentum said its request for information on cleaning and rehabilitation works in Gozo valleys was refused after the Ministry rejected the general request as insufficiently specific, and the party suspects the documents sought may not exist. The party had asked for details of the sites and dates of the works, technical and environmental assessments, expert advice, machinery and methods used, material removal and disposal, and inspection and monitoring reports. Momentum is asking what measures were taken to protect native biodiversity and prevent invasive alien species from returning, and its spokeswoman Graziella Spiteri said the public is entitled to an explanation of works affecting the natural environment.

item.title: Study finds many of Malta's mysterious cart ruts date to the Classical era
item.description: A new study of Malta's cart ruts has added weight to the argument that many of the parallel grooves cut into the islands' rocky landscape are far younger than some have claimed. Archaeologist Joel Grima of the University of Malta examined evidence relating to 2,628 individual tracks, drawing on three-dimensional models of 155 sites and digitised records from another 88, and concluded that a considerable proportion were formed between 700BC and AD 870, during the Phoenician, Punic, Roman and Byzantine eras. Grima said there is no solid evidence confirming a prehistoric date for any pair of Maltese cart ruts, though the possibility cannot at present be excluded. The work has been published in the Journal of Archaeological Science.

item.title: NGOs slam budget plan to end free public transport for third-country nationals
item.description: Moviment Graffitti, Rota, Friends of the Earth Malta and Solidarjetà said the government's plan to charge third-country nationals around €33 a month for public transport from next year is unjust and counterproductive, describing it as institutionalised discrimination that would create a two-tier transport system. The NGOs argued many third-country nationals are among the lowest-income and most socially marginalised residents while contributing through taxes, rent and work, and that charging them would do nothing to fix overcrowding, reliability and frequency. Maltese and EU nationals, and British nationals resident under the pre-Brexit arrangement, will continue to travel free.

item.title: Man charged with 25 thefts from vehicles remanded in custody
item.description: The police said a 41-year-old man was arraigned on Monday on a count of some 25 thefts from vehicles, reported between May and July in Cospicua, Senglea, Sliema and Żabbar. Items reported stolen included cash, electronic devices, tools, clothing and personal belongings, and in several cases the vehicles were also damaged. Following intensive investigations, the man was arrested and brought before Magistrate Dr Kevan Azzopardi. He pleaded not guilty, was denied bail and remains in custody.

item.title: Magistrate refuses to drop rape case after wife's plea to withdraw charges
item.description: A magistrate on Monday refused a request to drop rape charges against a man after his wife told the court she did not want her children to suffer any longer. The court rejected her request, citing concerns over her uncertainty after she appeared visibly confused while testifying and said she did not know whether she would return to live with the father of her children. The 56-year-old man, a support worker, was arraigned, pleaded not guilty and was remanded in custody. The woman reported him to the Domestic Violence Unit on 14 October, saying she had not previously understood that his behaviour was wrong because of her cultural background, and that she decided to report him after speaking to relatives.

item.title: Animal welfare chief to propose legal change to rehome confiscated animals before court cases end
item.description: Animal Welfare Commissioner Elliot Magro said his office is drafting a recommendation to change the law so that confiscated animals can be rehomed without waiting for criminal proceedings to conclude. Under the current system, animals seized in connection with court cases generally remain in the care of the Animal Welfare Department until the case is decided unless the owner consents to their transfer, so some spend much of their lives in cages while their chances of adoption diminish. Magro, who was particularly concerned about older dogs, said the proposal would create a separate procedure, including the possibility of an appeal, running alongside the criminal case.

item.title: Humanists Malta seeks middle ground in debate over secular Constitution
item.description: Humanists Malta is calling for a pluralist Constitution that recognises the Catholic Church's historical role in Malta while ensuring equal treatment for citizens regardless of their religion or belief. The organisation said the debate over a secular Constitution has often been presented as a choice between preserving Malta's Catholic identity and removing religion altogether. It highlighted Article 2, which establishes Roman Catholicism as Malta's religion and provides for compulsory religious teaching in State schools, and said the operative provisions should instead treat all citizens equally, with the State neutral towards all religions and beliefs.

item.title: €1 million project launched for training in the cultural and creative sectors
item.description: The Malta Council for the Arts has launched a €1 million project to improve skills and professional development in the cultural and creative sectors, co-funded by the European Social Fund Plus and running until December 2028 with a target of more than 470 people. It offers training grants of up to €2,000 for specialised training outside Malta or online, covering courses, masterclasses, conferences, seminars, workshops and networking, plus a free local programme of 18 modules across law for culture, sustainability and creative entrepreneurship at levels 3, 4 and 5 of the Malta Qualifications Framework. The local programme is open to public-sector employees, independent cultural and creative professionals and those working in the private sector or cultural organisations.
